name: Robin Thicke
hook: The singer of 'Blurred Lines', which a jury found had copied Marvin Gaye, and which Weird Al turned into a song about grammar.
blurb: Robin Thicke was born in Los Angeles in 1977, the son of the actors Alan Thicke and Gloria Loring. He started writing and producing songs for other R&B singers as a teenager, signed to Interscope at 16, and broke through with 'The Evolution of Robin Thicke' (2006). 'Blurred Lines' (2013), produced by Pharrell Williams with T.I., went to number one in America and was one of the best-selling singles ever. It was also widely criticised for lyrics and a video that many people called disrespectful to women, and Thicke later called a remark of his in GQ about degrading women a bad joke. Marvin Gaye's family sued in 2013, saying it copied Gaye's 'Got to Give It Up'. In 2015 a jury agreed, damages were set at $5.3 million plus royalties, and an appeals court, the Ninth Circuit, upheld it in 2018.
